sections.title: What is known, what is used
sections.content: You know *ha* + conditional from A2, the past conditional with *volna* from B1 Unit 20 and mixed conditionals from B1 Unit 35. This lesson uses them for one topic: what would happen, or would have happened, to a small language online. Example: *Ha nem fejlesztenénk magyar modelleket, nyelvünk a háttérbe szorulna.*

sections.title: Present and past
sections.content: Two patterns: *ha* + present conditional for what is unreal now (*Ha nem gyűjtenénk magyar szövegeket, a gépek nem tanulnák meg a nyelvünket.*), and *ha* + *volna* for the past (*Ha korábban elkezdtük volna, ma több adatunk lenne.*). Both clauses take the conditional; do not mix the plain present in the *ha*-clause with a conditional main clause.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: Ha nem gyűjtenénk magyar szövegeket, a gépek nem tanulnák meg a nyelvünket.
If we did not collect Hungarian texts, machines would not learn our language.
Ha korábban elkezdtük volna a gyűjtést, ma több adatunk lenne.
If we had started collecting earlier, we would have more data today.
Amennyiben az angol lesz az egyetlen nyelv a gépi kommunikációban, a kis nyelvek háttérbe szorulnak.
If English becomes the only language in machine communication, small languages will be pushed into the background.
